kernelIdea: n is even iff n = 2k for some integer k; odd iff n = 2k+1. Generally m | n iff n = mk for some k ∈ ℤ. Divisibility is an existence statement, so proving it means producing the k.

kernels.l1: Some piles share fairly between two people. Some leave one over.
kernels.l2: A number is even when it splits into two equal piles with nothing left over, and odd when exactly one is left over. That is the reason behind the last-digit trick.
kernels.l3: A number is even when it is a whole number of 2s with nothing left over, and odd when exactly one is left over. One number divides another when the second is a whole number of copies of the first — so proving it means producing that count.
kernels.l4: A whole number is even when it is twice another whole number, and odd when it is one more than that. More generally, m divides n when n is a whole number of copies of m. Divisibility is an existence claim, so proving it means producing that whole number.
kernels.l5: Divisibility is an existence claim: m divides n when some integer multiplies m to give n. The integer must be exhibited, and exhibiting it is the whole proof.
kernels.l6: Even, odd, and divides are all existential statements about integers; the quantifier structure is what dictates how they are proved and disproved.
kernels.l7: Parity and divisibility are existence statements about the integers: m divides n when some integer multiplies m to give n. Proving divisibility means exhibiting that integer and confirming it is one.
kernels.l8: Divisibility is the preorder on ℤ induced by the multiplicative monoid; it is the shadow of the ideal containment (n) ⊆ (m), which is how the notion generalizes to arbitrary rings.
